question: Does the rule-derived hand-value channel alone improve finite-budget outcomes over Unit hand prices when candidate board values, promotion gain, capture/type ordering, dynamic terms, and the fixed foe are held constant?
changed_premise: The newly completed integrated default-package sample showed that all eight root-owner pairs without a legal root drop tied, while the 24 with drops had more favorable observed utility/node reductions. The integrated contrast cannot attribute this to hand prices because board values, promotion gain, and capture-order values also changed. The earlier board-only factor held Unit hand prices and did not test this suspected channel.

roots.selection: Retain every deterministic legal-random root; no drop-count, outcome, price, promotion-exposure, action, or playability filtering; no replacement. Record root hand stock and legal-drop count; use complete results in all gates.

arms.fixed_foe: Unit board values, Unit hand values, zero promotion gains, default dynamic mobility and anchor-escape weights, identical in both arms.
arms.candidate_only_change: Both candidate arms use Unit board values (1000 per non-anchor, 0 anchor), zero promotion gains, identical Unit capture_order_value and type_value, ordinary default MoveOrderer, legal actions and complete history. Control uses Unit hand values (900 per non-anchor, 0 anchor); candidate substitutes only the rule-derived static hand_value_by_base_type. Both keep default dynamic-mobility weight 2, anchor-escape weight 5 and the same search settings. No optional StagedMovePicker, board-price, promotion, ordering, or opponent change.

analysis.primary: Pair rule-derived-hand-only candidate reward minus Unit-hand control by exact root and candidate owner against the fixed Unit foe; UNKNOWN contributes conservative [-1,+1] before subtraction.
analysis.robustness: Retain all planned cells. Report overall, both candidate owners, odd/even root prefix parity and leave-one-rule-seed-out bounds; preserve terminals, UNKNOWN and incomplete slots. Report drop-available versus no-drop root strata as exploratory only, never a replacement denominator.
analysis.cost: Report candidate nodes, completed depth, fallback and caller seconds separately; do not infer strength from node counts or wall time.
analysis.retain_rule: Retain a scoped hand-price candidate only if utility lower bounds are strictly positive overall, both owners, both parities and every leave-one-seed-out view, or median candidate-node reduction is at least 10% overall and in each owner/parity view while no matching utility lower bound is negative. Any pass does not authorize a default change or a universal hand-price claim.

integrity: Fresh generated rules, legal actions and complete GameSession history/replay, including promotion, drops and auxiliary state.
Assert the two candidate arms differ only in the declared hand price values; board and ordering values remain identical.
Preserve UNKNOWN, timeouts, failures and unstarted slots; no top-up, refit, solver, default change or AUX work.
Poll PRIMARY stop flags before each game; frozen hard cap 3600 seconds.

cost.threshold: Expected and capped run below 120 minutes.
cost.basis: The just-completed 64-game D3/8192/.5s integrated price-package run completed in 153.094 seconds; this 64-game run has the same search workload and adds no solver/training. All-in estimate 600 seconds including rule generation, history replay, analysis and variance.

decision_after: This single finite generated 5x5 hand-only contrast can select only whether to retain this scoped candidate for later independent transfer work. It cannot establish all-domain hand-price utility or justify a default change. If it fails, close this exact channel sample; do not repeat, top up, or silently redefine the target.
